notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a direct Driver over tektronix_func_gen:FuncGen, not a ScpiDriver. Every channel command is assembled from the channel number and a command word (SOURceN:..., OUTPutN:...; tektronix_func_gen.py:810-813 and 1044-1047), so a fixed command table cannot reproduce the lines. The driver uses FuncGen.get_settings/set_settings and the channel getters for the scalar settings, so the clone's model, impedance and amplitude/offset checks still run. The e-stop sends OUTPut1:STATe OFF and OUTPut2:STATe OFF through FuncGen.write. Every numeric setting (amplitude, offset, frequency of both channels) is Limit.operator_required because the clone selects the range from the connected model and the impedance setting, and the impedance cannot be read remotely (tektronix_func_gen.py:214-267, 1188-1201; README.md:197-200); site-limits.example.json is an example overlay for one bench, not a statement about a unit. NOT COVERED: the arbitrary-waveform arrays (get_custom_waveform/set_custom_waveform, binary transfers of 2 to 8192 or more 14-bit points; tektronix_func_gen.py:505-541 and 543-636) and the custom USER and built-in function shapes; the package serves the two channels' scalar settings, the frequency lock, the error queue and the waveform catalogue. The fake is an in-memory stand-in whose starting values are test data, not a recording of an instrument. No hardware was attached; the package is model-authored and unreviewed, and its hardware backend was never run. Evidence is contract_checked on the fake backend, never an MHS-Device level. gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
